notes.note: PR3's runtime-routes changes: the member caller gains an accountToken resolver (an account-tied personal token is held to its account's Project membership; a token that stops resolving mid-request acts for no one, never operator rules), and People's canHoldTokens now comes from DevicePairingService.canHoldPersonalToken (true for Tailscale-tied people and, with a local-account directory of the same issuer, account-tied people). The Personal access tokens section already says a local-account person can hold a token, held to the account's membership, valid only while the account exists, is enabled and has not signed out everywhere; canHoldTokens is described as whether a token can be made for them. Accurate.

Flagged for runtime-routes.ts (PR3: account-token member caller and canHoldTokens derivation). Its runtime-routes references describe route composition at a level these changes do not alter; no claim about Project membership callers or personal tokens.

Flagged for runtime-routes.ts. Its runtime-routes mentions (composition of route families, request principal resolution) are unaffected: PR3 only adds a token branch inside the existing member-caller wiring and changes how People computes canHoldTokens. No edit, so the generated station-docs-content bundle is unchanged.

Flagged for runtime-routes.ts. Its push claims (subscribe/unsubscribe need an identified paired device; a personal access token gets 403 device_pairing_required) are unchanged by PR3, which does not touch push routes; account-tied tokens are refused there exactly as Tailscale-tied ones.
Flagged for runtime-routes.ts. Its pairing and environment-reset claims are unaffected by the member-caller token branch and canHoldTokens derivation; it lists no People or token fields.
